title: A practical method for storage, preservation and transportation of anuran urine samples using filter paper for hormone analysis
author: Kumar, Sood, et al.

steps.title: Prepare assay reagents
steps.instruction: Gather the following reagents: monoclonal progesterone antibody (CL425, provided by Dr. Coralie Munro, University of California, USA), progesterone conjugated HRP, progesterone standards ranging from 200 pg/well to 0.39 pg/well (antibody cross‑reactivity 100% with progesterone and other metabolites as reported); polyclonal testosterone antibody (R156/7, provided by Dr. Coralie Munro, University of California, USA), testosterone conjugated HRP, testosterone standards ranging from 600 pg/well to 1.17 pg/well (cross‑reactivity 57.4% with dihydrotestosterone, <0.3% with androstenedione, <0.1% with androsterone, dihydroepiandrosterone, β‑estradiol and progesterone).

steps.title: Coat microtiter plate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of each diluted antibody in 0.05 M sodium bicarbonate buffer (pH 9.6) to the wells of a 96‑well Nunc MaxiSorp high‑binding plate (Thermo Fisher Scientific, UK). Seal the plate and incubate at 4 °C overnight in an airtight, humid container.

steps.title: Wash and add samples with HRP
steps.instruction: Wash the coated plate four times with wash buffer (0.15 M NaCl, 0.05 % Tween 20) using an automatic plate washer (Elx50; BioTek, USA) and dry the wells on a paper towel. Then add 50 µL of each urine sample or standard diluted in EIA buffer (0.1 M PBS containing 0.1 % BSA, pH 7.0) followed by 50 µL of the appropriate conjugated HRP. Incubate the plate at room temperature for 2 hours.

substeps.instruction: Wash plate 4× with 0.15 M NaCl, 0.05 % Tween 20 using Elx50 washer.
Dry wells on a paper towel.
Add 50 µL diluted urine sample or standard (0.1 M PBS, 0.1 % BSA, pH 7.0).
Incubate at room temperature for 2 h.

steps.title: Add substrate and develop color
steps.instruction: Re‑wash the plate as above, then add 50 µL of TMB/H₂O₂ solution (Genei, India) to each well. Incubate in the dark until the average optical density of the zero‑well reaches 0.8–1.0.

substeps.instruction: Wash plate 4× with wash buffer and dry.
Incubate in the dark until OD₀ reaches 0.8–1.0.

steps.title: Stop reaction and read absorbance
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 1 N HCl to each well to stop the reaction, then measure absorbance at 450 nm using a Multiskan Spectrophotometer (Thermo Multiskan Spectrum Plate Reader, version 2.4.2; Thermo Scientific, Finland).

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL 1 N HCl to each well.
Read absorbance at 450 nm with the Multiskan Spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Generate standard curve and calculate concentrations
steps.instruction: Plot absorbance versus known standard concentrations to create a standard curve; apply Beer‑Lambert’s law to determine hormone concentrations of unknown samples, expressing results as pg/µg creatinine.
